purpose: Risperidone is used to treat conditions like schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and irritability related to autism. It helps reduce symptoms such as hallucinations, delusions, mood swings, and aggressive behavior. It can help you think more clearly and feel more balanced day to day.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers called dopamine and serotonin to communicate between nerve cells. When these chemicals are out of balance, it can cause symptoms like hearing voices or extreme mood changes. Risperidone works by blocking certain receptors for these chemicals, helping to restore a healthier balance in the brain.
common_side_effects: You may feel drowsy or tired, especially when you first start taking it. Some people gain weight, feel restless, or notice stiffness or shakiness in their muscles. Other common effects include dizziness when standing up quickly, increased saliva, or mild stomach upset.
warnings: Risperidone can cause a serious movement disorder called tardive dyskinesia with long-term use — tell your doctor if you notice any unusual or uncontrolled movements. It may raise your blood sugar and cholesterol, so regular check-ups are important. Elderly patients with dementia should use this medication with caution, as it carries an increased risk of stroke. Avoid alcohol, and tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
typical_dosing: Dosing is very individual and depends on your condition. For adults with schizophrenia, a common starting dose is 1 to 2 mg once or twice daily, slowly increasing to a typical range of 4 to 8 mg per day. Your doctor will find the lowest dose that works best for you, so never change your dose without talking to them first.
